sheets.title: Basics & Complexity
sheets.description: Before a clever structure, check whether one pass and a clear complexity target are enough.

patterns.recognitionSignal: The answer is a sum, count, min, or max.
patterns.firstQuestion: Can I update the answer while I scan?

patterns.recognitionSignal: The position itself carries information.
patterns.typicalProblems: find the duplicate, first missing positive
patterns.firstQuestion: Can the value be placed at its own index?

patterns.recognitionSignal: The interviewer expects a target before code.
patterns.firstQuestion: What is the best time and extra memory I can justify?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Empty input, one element, duplicates, and overflow.
patterns.firstQuestion: Which input breaks the happy path?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Extra memory may be forbidden.
patterns.firstQuestion: Am I allowed a second array?

patterns.recognitionSignal: The problem cares which duplicate or index survives.
patterns.firstQuestion: Do I keep the first occurrence or the last?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Any problem where the optimal idea is not obvious yet.
patterns.typicalProblems: two sum by nested loops, all pairs
patterns.firstQuestion: What is the slow but correct answer, and where does it repeat work?

patterns.recognitionSignal: The input is a single integer and you need its digits.
patterns.typicalProblems: reverse integer, palindrome number, happy number
patterns.firstQuestion: Can n % 10 and Math.floor(n / 10) peel one digit per step?

patterns.recognitionSignal: n is given in the constraints.
patterns.typicalProblems: n <= 1e5 means O(n log n); n <= 20 means 2^n
patterns.firstQuestion: Which complexity class fits inside about 1e8 simple operations?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Many primality or divisor questions up to n.
patterns.firstQuestion: Can I cross out multiples once instead of testing each number?

patterns.recognitionSignal: A formula replaces a loop.
patterns.typicalProblems: trailing zeroes, power of two, sum 1..n
patterns.firstQuestion: Is there a known identity, like counting factors of 5?

decisionTree.thinkFirst: Place each value at its index
Pick a pattern sheet and start again
Aim for O(n log n) or better
Say the brute force, then remove repeated work

workflow.action: Read the constraints and the output format before writing code
workflow.mistake: Jumping to code without knowing n or the value range

workflow.action: Translate n into a complexity budget out loud
workflow.mistake: Writing O(n^2) when n is 1e5

workflow.action: State the brute force in one sentence
workflow.mistake: Staying silent while searching for the clever idea

workflow.action: Remove repeated work to reach the target complexity
workflow.mistake: Optimising code that is already within budget

workflow.action: Dry-run an empty, a single, and a large input
workflow.mistake: Only testing the sample input

sheets.title: Sorting Algorithms
sheets.description: Sort only when order unlocks a simpler scan, merge, or greedy choice.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need a total order and n is large enough that O(n log n) is acceptable.
patterns.typicalProblems: sort colors, kth via sort, merge intervals
patterns.firstQuestion: Does a later linear scan become obvious after sorting?

patterns.recognitionSignal: The order is not numeric: intervals, strings, or multi-key records.
patterns.typicalProblems: merge intervals, largest number, meeting order
patterns.firstQuestion: Which field must be ordered first, and which is the tie-break?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Values sit in a small known range.
patterns.typicalProblems: sort colors, relative sort, top-k by count
patterns.firstQuestion: Is the value range small enough to count instead of compare?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Exactly three categories must be partitioned in place.
patterns.firstQuestion: Can low, mid, and high pointers separate the three groups?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Two or more inputs are already ordered.
patterns.typicalProblems: merge sorted arrays, merge k lists
patterns.firstQuestion: Am I merging two runs, or k runs that need a heap?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Duplicates, neighbors, or pairs become adjacent after ordering.
patterns.firstQuestion: After sorting, can two pointers or one pass finish the problem?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need the kth element, not a fully sorted array.
patterns.firstQuestion: Can I partition around a pivot and recurse into one side only?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Count inversions or pairs while sorting.
patterns.typicalProblems: reverse pairs, count of smaller after self
patterns.firstQuestion: Can I count cross pairs during the merge step?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Values are 1..n (or 0..n) and indexes can hold them.
patterns.firstQuestion: Can I swap each value into index value - 1?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Order elements by how often they appear.
patterns.typicalProblems: sort characters by frequency, top k words
patterns.typicalComplexity: O(n log n) or bucket O(n)
patterns.firstQuestion: Count first, then sort the keys or bucket by count?

patterns.recognitionSignal: A second array or a rank decides the order.
patterns.typicalProblems: relative sort array, custom sort string
patterns.firstQuestion: Can I map each value to its rank, then compare ranks?

decisionTree.signal: Order makes neighbors or pairs obvious?

decisionTree.thinkFirst: Heap merge, not a full sort
Sort pairs of value and index

workflow.action: Ask whether order unlocks a simpler scan
workflow.mistake: Sorting by reflex and losing the original indexes

workflow.action: Pick the sort: comparison, counting, or partition
workflow.mistake: Using a comparison sort on a tiny value range

workflow.action: Write the comparator and its tie-break
workflow.mistake: Comparators that are not consistent (a < b and b < a)

workflow.action: Finish with a single linear pass
workflow.mistake: Nested loops after the sort

workflow.action: Test duplicates, negatives, and already-sorted input
workflow.mistake: Forgetting stability when ties matter

sheets.title: Recursion
sheets.description: Trust the function on a smaller input. Every recursive answer is a base case plus one step that uses the smaller answer.

patterns.recognitionSignal: The answer for n is built from the answer for n - 1 or n / 2.
patterns.firstQuestion: What is the smallest input I can answer directly?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Work happens before or after the recursive call.
patterns.typicalProblems: print 1..n, print n..1, reverse a list
patterns.firstQuestion: Should I act before or after the call returns?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Split the input in halves and combine.
patterns.firstQuestion: How do I combine the two half answers?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Each node asks its children, then combines.
patterns.typicalProblems: max depth, same tree, invert tree
patterns.firstQuestion: What does each child return to its parent?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Every element is either in or out of the answer.
patterns.firstQuestion: What are the two calls, and what changes between them?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Build strings or lists that must stay valid.
patterns.firstQuestion: Which constraint lets me stop a branch early?

patterns.recognitionSignal: The same arguments are computed many times.
patterns.typicalProblems: climbing stairs, decode ways, word break
patterns.firstQuestion: Which arguments define the state, and can I cache them?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Peel one character or a prefix each call.
patterns.firstQuestion: Do I pass an index instead of slicing the string?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Grammar-like input such as nested brackets.
patterns.firstQuestion: Can each call parse one level and return where it stopped?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Deep input risks a stack overflow.
patterns.typicalProblems: tree traversals, flood fill on a big grid
patterns.firstQuestion: What would the explicit stack hold if I removed the recursion?

decisionTree.signal: Answer for n uses the answer for n - 1?
Output must stay valid while building?

workflow.action: Write the function signature and what it promises
workflow.mistake: Starting with the loop body instead of the contract

workflow.action: Write the base case first
workflow.mistake: Missing a base case and recursing forever

workflow.action: Assume the smaller call works and use its result
workflow.mistake: Tracing every level in your head

workflow.action: Draw the recursion tree to find repeated work
workflow.mistake: Exponential time from overlapping calls

workflow.action: State time and stack depth
workflow.mistake: Ignoring the O(n) stack space

sheets.title: Arrays & Hashing
sheets.description: Use this before solving an array problem: identify the signal, choose the smallest useful tool, then confirm the expected complexity.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need to inspect every element or compute one overall value.
patterns.firstQuestion: Ask: Can I solve this by visiting each element once?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need first/last index, existence, or a matching value.
patterns.firstQuestion: Use an early return when the answer is known.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Question talks about positions, index parity, or neighbor relationships.
patterns.firstQuestion: Think about i, i + 1, and i - 1 before using extra data.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need to rotate, shift, or directly change elements.
patterns.firstQuestion: Track temporary values carefully.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Sorted array, pair/triplet, opposite ends, in-place removal, or compare mirrors.
patterns.typicalProblems: two sum sorted, palindrome, remove duplicates, move zeroes
patterns.firstQuestion: Ask: Can two indexes shrink the search or separate read/write roles?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need frequency or fast lookup of a value to information.
patterns.typicalProblems: Two Sum, counts, majority, intersection with duplicates
patterns.firstQuestion: Ask: Would knowing something about a value already seen save a scan?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need uniqueness or fast membership only.
patterns.firstQuestion: Map if you need counts or information; Set if you only need membership.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Contiguous subarray or window has exactly K elements.
patterns.typicalProblems: max/min sum, max count, window target
patterns.firstQuestion: Window size is fixed: add right, remove left.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Contiguous segment must be longest or shortest while satisfying a condition.
patterns.typicalProblems: sum >= target, at most K zeros/odds
patterns.firstQuestion: Expand until valid/invalid, then shrink while possible.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Many range sums or subarray-sum reasoning.
patterns.typicalProblems: range sum, pivot, subarray sum K
patterns.firstQuestion: Can a cumulative value make each range or subarray query O(1)?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need the best sum of a contiguous subarray.
patterns.firstQuestion: At each element: extend the current best or start fresh?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Order can simplify duplicates, neighbors, merging, pairs, or greedy choices.
patterns.firstQuestion: Before sorting, ask whether order unlocks a simpler linear scan.

patterns.recognitionSignal: After sorting, pair/triplet target problems become monotonic.
patterns.firstQuestion: Sorting first often removes the need for nested lookup.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need to modify the same array and return a compact prefix.
patterns.firstQuestion: Separate the index you read from the index you write.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need to count subarrays with an exact sum.
patterns.firstQuestion: Store how many times each prefix sum has appeared.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Numbers have a constrained value range tied to indexes.
patterns.firstQuestion: Ask whether each value can be placed at its correct index.

decisionTree.signal: Just scan, count, sum, max, or min?
Sorted + pair, mirrored ends, or in-place?
Repeated range sums or subarray-sum logic?
Could sorting make duplicates, pairs, or neighbors easier?

workflow.action: Read constraints + output before coding
workflow.mistake: Jumping to code without understanding limits

workflow.action: Circle the trigger words: sorted, contiguous, in-place, frequency, k
workflow.mistake: Choosing a pattern from the topic name only

workflow.action: State the pattern aloud
workflow.mistake: Saying only 'I'll use a loop'

workflow.action: Give brute force first, then optimize
workflow.mistake: Pretending the optimized idea is obvious

workflow.action: Test one normal + one edge case
workflow.mistake: Only testing the happy path

sheets.title: Hashing
sheets.description: Trade memory for time. A map answers 'have I seen this, and what did I learn about it' in O(1) on average.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Need a pair that sums or matches a target.
patterns.typicalProblems: two sum, pairs with difference k
patterns.firstQuestion: For each value, which partner would finish the answer?

patterns.recognitionSignal: The answer depends on how often values appear.
patterns.typicalProblems: valid anagram, majority element, first unique char
patterns.firstQuestion: Count first, then read the counts?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Items that share a signature belong together.
patterns.firstQuestion: What canonical key makes equal items collide?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Only existence matters.
patterns.firstQuestion: Do I need counts, or is membership enough?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Distance between equal values matters.
patterns.typicalProblems: contains duplicate II, longest substring without repeat
patterns.firstQuestion: Store the latest index of each value?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Count subarrays with an exact sum or remainder.
patterns.typicalProblems: subarray sum equals k, subarray sums divisible by k
patterns.firstQuestion: How many earlier prefixes equal current - k?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Two sequences must map one-to-one.
patterns.firstQuestion: Do I need maps in both directions?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Find runs without sorting.
patterns.firstQuestion: Start counting only from values whose predecessor is missing?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Compare frequency shapes, not values.
patterns.typicalProblems: determine if two strings are close, unique occurrences
patterns.firstQuestion: Do I compare the multiset of counts?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Substrings or rows used as keys.
patterns.typicalProblems: repeated DNA sequences, equal row and column pairs
patterns.firstQuestion: Can I join the items into a string key, or hash a window?

workflow.action: Say what you would look up if lookups were free
workflow.mistake: Using a map without knowing the key

workflow.action: Choose map (needs info) or set (needs existence)
workflow.mistake: Storing counts you never read

workflow.action: Define the key precisely (sorted string, tuple, prefix)
workflow.mistake: Keys that collide for different items

workflow.action: Decide when to insert: before or after the check
workflow.mistake: Matching an element with itself

workflow.action: State average versus worst case and the memory cost
workflow.mistake: Claiming O(1) worst case

sheets.title: Binary Search
sheets.description: Use it when the answer space is ordered and each guess discards half of it.

patterns.recognitionSignal: A sorted array and you need an exact value or its index.
patterns.firstQuestion: Is the array sorted, and do I need the leftmost or rightmost hit?

patterns.recognitionSignal: You need the first position where a predicate becomes true.
patterns.firstQuestion: Can I define a monotonic true/false predicate?

patterns.recognitionSignal: A sorted array was rotated, so one side is still sorted.
patterns.firstQuestion: Which half is still sorted, and is the target inside it?

patterns.recognitionSignal: You binary search the answer, not an index.
patterns.typicalProblems: koko, capacity to ship, split array
patterns.firstQuestion: If mid is feasible, should I search lower or higher?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Rows and columns are sorted, or each row is sorted.
patterns.firstQuestion: Can I treat the matrix as one sorted array, or walk from a corner?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Neighbors tell you which direction increases.
patterns.firstQuestion: Does the midpoint's neighbor point left or right?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Sorted input with duplicates; need a range.
patterns.firstQuestion: Run two bound searches: first >= target and first > target?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Find the largest integer x with f(x) <= target.
patterns.typicalProblems: sqrt(x), valid perfect square, arranging coins
patterns.firstQuestion: What are lo and hi, and is f monotonic?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Pairs are adjacent except one element.
patterns.typicalProblems: single element in a sorted array
patterns.firstQuestion: Does the pair start at an even index left of the single?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Median or kth across two sorted arrays.
patterns.firstQuestion: Which cut makes every left value <= every right value?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Split or distribute so the worst part is as small as possible.
patterns.typicalProblems: split array largest sum, ship packages, bouquets
patterns.firstQuestion: Given a cap, can I greedily check feasibility in O(n)?

decisionTree.signal: Sorted and looking for a value?
Need the first true in a yes/no range?
One half of a rotated array is sorted?
Min or max value that still works?

decisionTree.thinkFirst: Check the mid update and inclusive bounds

decisionTree.signal: Integer root or largest x with f(x) <= t?

decisionTree.thinkFirst: Binary search on the cap plus a greedy check

decisionTree.signal: Two sorted arrays and a median?
decisionTree.thinkFirst: Partition search on the smaller array

workflow.action: Find the monotonic property before searching

workflow.action: Choose the search space: an index or an answer value
workflow.mistake: Searching indexes when the answer is a value range

workflow.action: Fix the loop invariant: lo <= hi or lo < hi
workflow.mistake: Mixing invariants and looping forever

workflow.action: Write the feasibility check as its own function
workflow.mistake: Inlining a buggy greedy check

workflow.action: Test one element, two elements, and the target at each end
workflow.mistake: Off-by-one at the boundaries

sheets.title: Two Pointers
sheets.description: Two indexes move toward each other or in the same direction when the array has order or a pair structure.

patterns.recognitionSignal: A sorted array and a pair target.
patterns.typicalProblems: two sum II, container with most water
patterns.firstQuestion: If the sum is too small, which pointer must move?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Read and write, or a slow and fast scan of one array.
patterns.firstQuestion: What does the slow pointer represent when the fast pointer moves?

patterns.recognitionSignal: A linked list cycle, or the middle of a list.
patterns.firstQuestion: If fast moves twice as fast, where do they meet?

patterns.recognitionSignal: A pair becomes a triplet once the array is sorted.
patterns.firstQuestion: After fixing one index, can two pointers finish the rest?

patterns.pattern: Shrink a window from both sides
patterns.recognitionSignal: The answer is a pair of boundaries, not every subarray.
patterns.firstQuestion: Which side is the limiting height or value?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Values must be rearranged around a pivot or condition.
patterns.firstQuestion: Which region is already correct, and which index is next?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Two sorted inputs combine into one.
patterns.firstQuestion: Fill from the back when merging in place?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Reverse a string, an array, or words.
patterns.firstQuestion: Swap ends until the pointers meet?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Is one sequence inside another in order?
patterns.firstQuestion: Advance the short pointer only on a match?

patterns.recognitionSignal: A palindrome check that tolerates one mismatch.
patterns.firstQuestion: On the first mismatch, try skipping either side once?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Pair the lightest with the heaviest.
patterns.typicalProblems: boats to save people, k-sum pairs
patterns.firstQuestion: If the heaviest cannot pair with the lightest, can it pair with anyone?

decisionTree.signal: Need every subarray, not a pair?

decisionTree.signal: Merging two sorted arrays in place?
One sequence inside another in order?

sheets.title: Sliding Window
sheets.description: The answer is a contiguous segment. Expand the right edge and shrink the left edge.

patterns.recognitionSignal: The segment length is exactly k.
patterns.typicalProblems: max sum of size k, average of size k
patterns.firstQuestion: Add the new right element and drop the element that fell out.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Longest segment that still satisfies a constraint.
patterns.typicalProblems: longest substring without repeat, at most k zeros
patterns.firstQuestion: Expand while valid. When invalid, shrink until valid again.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Shortest segment that reaches a target.
patterns.typicalProblems: minimum window substring, shortest subarray with sum
patterns.firstQuestion: Shrink while the window still meets the target, and record the best.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Count segments with a property, not just the best one.
patterns.firstQuestion: Can at most k minus at most k-1 give exactly k?

patterns.recognitionSignal: The constraint is about character or value counts.
patterns.firstQuestion: What count makes the window valid, and when do I shrink?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Each step needs the min or max inside the current window.
patterns.firstQuestion: Can a deque drop indexes that can never be the answer?

patterns.recognitionSignal: Longest window with at most k kinds of values.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Count windows with exactly k of something.

patterns.recognitionSignal: Count subarrays with product below k.

patterns.recognitionSignal: The array wraps around.

decisionTree.signal: Exactly k, and at most k is easy?
